name: NuTeV
summary: NuTeV was a high-energy Fermilab neutrino-scattering experiment using a sign-selected beam and an upgraded iron-scintillator detector descended from CCFR.
physics_targets: Weak mixing angle and electroweak consistency
Rare processes and heavy neutral-particle searches
detection_principle: Separate neutrino and antineutrino beams illuminated a sampling calorimeter followed by a toroidal muon spectrometer. Ratios of neutral-current to charged-current interactions probed electroweak couplings with reduced common uncertainties.

results.summary: Reported an on-shell weak-mixing-angle determination that differed from the then Standard Model expectation; interpretation is sensitive to nuclear, parton-distribution and radiative corrections.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
